title: La rezadora
goal: Be invited to a novena and know what is expected
culture: A novena is nine nights of prayer for somebody who died, and the rezadora leads it. Going is a kindness to the family and nobody will test your faith at the door. Do not turn up with flowers or wine — there is coffee and bread and that is the form.

beats.es: Buenas noches. ¿Usted es el vecino nuevo? Estamos rezando aquí al lado.
beats.good: Nine nights, one for each, ending on the ninth with the biggest one. Knowing that is knowing what you are being invited to.

beats.es: Nueve, sí. Desde que se nos fue don Ramón.
ok: y a que hora a las siete
a que hora a las siete
beats.good: Seven, after work and before the heat drops. It will start at ten past and nobody minds.

beats.es: A las siete. Y véngase, aunque sea un ratito.
beats.good: Ask, and the answer will be no hace falta — there is no need. Ask anyway: not asking is what would be rude.

beats.es: No hace falta nada, mi hijo. Con que venga, con eso basta.
beats.en: That’s enough, then. I’ll be there.
beats.good: Con eso basta — that is enough. Turning up IS the gift, and ahí llego is a promise you should keep.
